newsitem.title: GERMANY: Metro sees improved profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Metro sees improved profit in 1997.

text.p: German retail giant Metro AG said on Monday it expected to boost profits this year after the recently-merged group posted a first group profit on ordinary activities of 1.1 billion marks in 1996.
The company, in a statement announcing annual results, said that although 1997 would be another difficult year for German retailers, management still expected "a positive development in the company".
Metro added that it expected sales to grow by at least three billion marks from last year's 62 billion marks and profits would advance.

"This result expectation is based on our conviction that we will improve results in our business areas, lossmakers will no longer be part of the group and that we still have further merger synergies," chief executive Klaus Wiegandt said.
Metro was created last summer out of the merger of three big German store groups.
